hints: Focus on the test result first, a gas that turns blue litmus red must be an acidic gas like $\text{HCl}$ or $\text{SO}_2$.
Recall which reagents convert an alcohol like ethanol into a chloroalkane and release $\text{HCl}$ as a steamy acidic by-product.
Compare the powerful chlorinating agents $\text{SOCl}_2$ and $\text{PCl}_5$ with simple chloride ions or dilute acid, and check which two give a rapid acidic gas.
walkthrough:
**Understand what we are testing for**

Think like a detective. We add each reagent to ethanol and we want rapid fizzing of an acidic gas.

Acidic gases to remember:
$$\text{HCl (hydrogen chloride) and SO}_2 \text{ (sulfur dioxide) turn blue litmus red}$$

**Check reagents 1 and 2**

Aqueous $\text{KCl}$ just provides $\text{Cl}^-$ ions in water. Chloride ions alone will not attack ethanol, so no reaction and no gas.

Dilute $\text{HCl}$ also does not rapidly convert ethanol to chloroethane. That substitution needs concentrated conditions and heating with a catalyst, so no rapid acidic gas is evolved.

**Check reagents 3 and 4, the chlorinating agents**

Both thionyl chloride and phosphorus(V) chloride rapidly replace the $\text{-OH}$ group of an alcohol with $\text{-Cl}$.

With thionyl chloride:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{SOCl}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} + \text{SO}_2 + \text{HCl}$$
Both $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$ are acidic gases.

With phosphorus(V) chloride:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{PCl}_5 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} + \text{POCl}_3 + \text{HCl}$$
Steamy $\text{HCl}$ gas is evolved rapidly.

So only 3 and 4 fit the description.

options.A: Incorrect. Aqueous KCl gives no reaction with ethanol, and dilute HCl does not rapidly form chloroethane or release HCl gas. Students sometimes think any source of Cl will make a chloroalkane, but Cl- needs a powerful reagent to replace -OH.
options.B: Incorrect. Reagent 3 does work, but reagent 1 does not. Aqueous KCl is unreactive toward ethanol, so this pair cannot both give an acidic gas.
options.C: Incorrect. Reagent 4 does work, but reagent 2 does not. Dilute HCl is too dilute and the conditions too mild for rapid substitution of ethanol, so no rapid evolution of acidic gas occurs. The trap is confusing dilute HCl with conc. HCl / ZnCl2 conditions.
options.D: Correct. Both liquid SOCl2 and solid PCl5 rapidly convert ethanol to chloroethane with evolution of HCl gas (and SO2 from SOCl2). Both gases are acidic and turn blue litmus red, giving the observed rapid positive test.
